title.narrative: Professionalization and capacity buildg of public proc. in Djibouti

description.narrative: The proposed operation comes in response to a request from the Government of Djibouti (the Secrétaire Général of the Ministry of Finance (MoF), specifically) to support them in implementing a sustainable program for procurement capacity building and professionalization. In summary, the proposal aims to help the government make the procurement law passed in 2009 more effective by addressing weaknesses in its implementation as evidenced by: (i) a lack of awareness of the new procurement law among public entities; (ii) delays in contact signing due to administrative procedures; (iii) delayed procurement implementation under Bank-funded projects as a result of delayed bid opening; (iv) a lack of publicly available procurement plans to enable broader private sector participation in tenders; and (v) weak capacity in procurement implementation and management (as highlighted in the 2011 Country Portfolio Performance Review). The two components of the proposed US $350k IDF are to develop a (i) sustainable national training and capacity building program and (ii) public procurement portal. The capacity building program activities will include a needs assessment, train the trainers modules, a capacity building program for Djiboutian public procurement stakeholders, cross-fertilization clinics to share knowledge among practitioners, logistical support to the MoF in carrying out the capacity building, and study tours. The portal will help improve the governance framework of the country and promote transparency in public procurement. It will allow procuring entities to easily publish their bidding announcements and awards, increase competition by better informing the private sector of public bidding opportunities, empower the regulatory body by providing needed information for its oversight and reports, and help citizens to better monitor government activities in procurement.
